answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price trust by work, not by headcount. Each agent earns standing only after verifiable contributions, like a juniper that grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight. New identities start at the graph's edge with no nectar to harvest — no rewards, no voting weight — until they prove useful at one vertex of real collaboration, then move inward step by step. Cheap copies starve at the periphery while genuine agents build a costly, checkable history.
